When the memory is full, the status line shows MEMORY FULL.

REPEAT EVERY and AFTER SEND work as the other value rows do: click the dial, turn it to change the value, and click again.

The device saves the memories when you leave the settings screen.

docs.title: Menu
docs.text:
The menu is a top list and three lists it opens: RECEIVE, ON AIR and STATS. Each row shows the name of a screen or a list. A > at the right end marks a row that opens a list. Under the rows, a line tells you what the selected row holds, and a dimmer line names the work the idea came from.

To open the menu, press F4 (MENU) on the KEYER screen. F4 (BACK) on any other screen opens the list that holds that screen, with its row selected. SETTINGS is the exception: BACK returns to the screen you opened it from.

docs.title: The top list
docs.text:
Row Opens Page RESUME The practice you left, where you left it. After you turn the device on, it starts the last practice you opened again from the start. The right end names the practice. The row shows once you have opened a practice. See below RECEIVE The list of receive drills. Receive drills ON AIR The list of on-air practice: activations, the hunt and ragchews. See below TIMING A zoomed timing tape and histograms of your keying. Timing STATS The list of your statistics. See below SETTINGS Every setting. Settings SYSTEM Version, hardware checks and battery. System

The header of the top list shows your callsign.

docs.title: RECEIVE
docs.text:
Row Opens KOCH The Koch drill. The right end shows your level, such as LEVEL 12. WORDS The words drill. CALLS The callsigns drill. NINJA Morse, then the word spoken. HEAD The head-copy ladder. The right end shows your rung, such as RUNG 3.

See Receive drills.

docs.title: ON AIR
docs.text: Row Opens Page POTA Activate a park and work a pileup. Activate a park or summit SOTA Activate a summit and work a pileup. Activate a park or summit HUNT Hunt activators on parks and summits. Hunt CHEW Listen to two stations ragchew. Ragchew QUIZ A ragchew with a question about each over. Ragchew RADIO What the decoder board of the Pro model hears, or what a computer sends as MIDI notes, decoded. This row shows only when DECODER BOARD is ON or USB OUT is not OFF. Radio

docs.title: STATS
docs.text: Row Opens Page LETTERS Your accuracy for each character, and your mixups. Letters PROGRESS Practice time and totals for recent sessions. Progress

docs.title: Paused practice
docs.text:
When you leave a drill, an activation, the hunt or a ragchew, it pauses. It keeps its log, transcript and score while the device is on. The RESUME row shows at the top of the top list, and the practice's own row shows PAUSED. Click either row to go on.

The device remembers the last practice you opened, even after you turn it off. With nothing paused, RESUME starts that practice again from the start. KOCH starts at your level, and HEAD at your rung. The footer then reads START YOUR LAST PRACTICE AGAIN.

Only one practice pauses at a time. When you start a different one, the paused one ends.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1 (SET) Opens the settings at the KEYER section. F2, F3 Nothing. F4 (BACK) In the top list, opens the KEYER screen. In another list, opens the top list. Dial turn Moves the selection up or down. Dial click Opens the selected row. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more.

docs.title: Progress
docs.text:
The PROGRESS screen shows your practice over recent sessions. A session is one time the device is on, from turn on to turn off. The device has no clock, so sessions take the place of days.

Open STATS in the menu, then PROGRESS. The header shows how many sessions the device keeps, such as 12 SESSIONS.

The device keeps the last 32 sessions. A session starts to count at the first thing you do, so a turn on with no practice does not take a place. When all 32 places are full, a new session replaces the oldest.

docs.title: What counts
docs.text: Column What it counts TIME Time while you key, on any screen, and while a drill, ragchew, POTA, SOTA or HUNT sends to you. A gap between the two counts when it is 60 seconds or less. SENT Characters you sent on the key, on any screen. COPY Percent right in receive drills and ragchew quizzes. QSOS QSOs you logged when you activate or hunt.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text:
The chart shows the last 14 sessions, the newest at the right. NOW marks the session in progress.

  • A filled bar shows the minutes of practice in that session.
  • A hollow square shows the COPY percent in that session. A session with no receive practice has no square.

The scale at the left shows the most minutes in the chart, 10 minutes or more.

The table under the chart has two rows:

  • NOW: this session. - means nothing counted yet.
  • LAST n: all the sessions the device keeps, added together.

Time shows as minutes, such as 25M, or as hours and minutes, such as 1H05. - in COPY means no receive practice.

Before your first session, the chart says NOTHING YET: START KEYING.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1 (SET) Opens the settings at the RECEIVE section. F4 (BACK) there returns to this screen. F3 Nothing. F2 (LTRS) Opens Letters. F4 (BACK) Opens the STATS list of the menu. Dial turn Changes the focused header value. See Header values. Dial click Moves the focus to the next header value. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more.

docs.title: Radio
docs.text:
The RADIO screen shows Morse code the device hears, as text: from the decoder board of the Pro model, which listens to the audio of a radio, or from a computer that sends it as MIDI notes, such as Vail.

Open it from the ON AIR list of the menu, or hold F3 on the KEYER screen. The menu shows RADIO while DECODER BOARD is ON or USB OUT is not OFF.

No one has tried PocketCW on a Pro model yet. The board parts of this screen follow the vendor firmware, but they are not tested on a board.

docs.title: Turn the decoder board on
docs.text:
1. Open the settings, and go to the DEVICE section. See Settings.
  2. Set DECODER BOARD to ON. The device powers the decoder board.
  3. The ON AIR list of the menu now shows the RADIO row. Open it.

On a model without a decoder board, keep DECODER BOARD OFF. The setting is OFF by default.

Connect the radio's audio to the AUX1 port of the decoder board. Headphones or a powered speaker go in AUX2. The VOLUME setting also sets the volume of AUX2.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text:
The top line shows the state of the board, or MIDI IN while DECODER BOARD is OFF:

Item Meaning MIDI IN DECODER BOARD is OFF, so the text comes only from MIDI notes. BOARD OK or NO REPLY BOARD OK: the board announced itself after it got power. NO REPLY: the board did not announce itself yet. FIL n The filter setting of the board, 0 to 2. NR n The noise reduction level of the board, 0 to 6. nnWPM The speed of the Morse code the device hears. Two dashes stand in for the number before the first speed reading. ERR n Data errors on the link to the board. This item shows only after an error.

Under the top line, nine lines show the text the device decodes.

The device decodes only while the RADIO screen is open, or on every screen while USB OUT is RADIO. With the board on and MIDI notes coming in, both go to the same lines. See USB keyboard. Each time decoding starts, the decoder starts at 20 WPM and then follows the speed it hears, from 5 to 60 WPM. The text stays when you leave the screen.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1 (SET) Opens the settings at the DEVICE section. F4 (BACK) there returns to this screen. F2 (FILT) Changes the filter setting of the board: 0, 1, 2, then 0 again. Only while DECODER BOARD is ON. F3 (NR) Changes the noise reduction level of the board: 0 to 6, then 0 again. Only while DECODER BOARD is ON. F4 (BACK) Opens the ON AIR list of the menu. Dial turn Changes the focused header value. See Header values. Dial click Moves the focus to the next header value. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more.

docs.title: Ragchew
docs.text:
In a ragchew, two stations hold a full QSO for you to copy. One station calls CQ, the other answers, and they trade signal reports, names, cities (QTH), rigs, antennas, weather (WX), years licensed, ages and jobs. Then they sign off with 73, and the station that called CQ sends the last E E. After 11 overs, two new stations start a new QSO.

Each station has its own way to word its overs, such as NAME or OP, and HW? or HW CPY?. Most stations are in the US. Some are in Canada or other countries: these send temperatures in Celsius and antenna heights in meters, and a station outside the US and Canada sends a city with no state. It adds its country when the line is short enough, such as QTH ROME ITALY.

Open ON AIR in the menu, then CHEW or QUIZ. The header shows which one:

Kind What you do CHEW Listen. The text of each over shows after the over ends. QUIZ After an over, answer a question about it. The device scores your answer like a receive drill.

The stations send at CHAR SPEED, with FARNSWORTH spacing when you set it. With FIST set to HUMAN, each station keys with its own small timing errors. The two stations send at slightly different pitches. See Settings.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text: The screen shows each over in a list: the sender's callsign at the left of the first line, then the text. The two stations show in two colors. Text that you have not been shown yet shows as a row of dashes.

docs.title: CHEW
docs.text:
CHEW SHOWS in the DRILLS section of the settings sets when text shows:

  • WHOLE OVER: each over shows after it ends.
  • EACH LINE: each line shows after it ends.

The footer repeats this choice.

docs.title: QUIZ
docs.text:
After an over that holds a fact, the screen asks one question, such as:

SENDER'S CALL?, RST?, NAME?, QTH CITY?, RIG?, POWER IN WATTS?, ANTENNA?, WX?, TEMPERATURE?, YEARS LICENSED?, AGE? or JOB?

  1. The state at the right of your answer shows YOUR TURN. Start to key the answer within 10 seconds.
  2. While you key, the state shows KEYING. When you stop keying for three word gaps, your answer ends.
  3. The device shows the answer as sent, your copy with each character marked, and the score. The text of the over shows too. After 2.5 seconds the next over plays.

If you do not start to key within 10 seconds, the answer counts as missed. To hear the over again, key ? alone as your answer. The sign off overs have no question.

The footer shows your score for this session.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Control Action F1 (SET) Pauses and opens the settings at the DRILLS section. F4 (BACK) there returns, and the current over plays again at the new settings. F2 (AGN) While an over plays or waits for your answer: sends the over again from its start. Blank while paused. F3 (STOP or GO) Pauses, or starts again from the start of the current over. F4 (BACK) Pauses and opens the ON AIR list of the menu. Click CHEW or QUIZ, or RESUME, to go on from the start of the current over. Dial turn Changes the focused header value. See Header values. Dial click Moves the focus to the next header value. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key QUIZ: keys your answer. CHEW: nothing more.

Quiz scores also go to Letters and Progress.

docs.title: Receive drills
docs.text:
In a receive drill, the device sends a group of characters, and you key back what you copied. The device then shows the group with each character marked right or wrong.

To start, open RECEIVE in the menu, then the drill. The header shows the name of the drill. For a ragchew to copy, see Ragchew in the ON AIR list.

Drill What the device sends KOCH Groups of 5 characters from the Koch characters of your level. WORDS One common word or abbreviation heard on the air, such as QTH, 5NN or <BK>. CALLS One US callsign. NINJA One word from the content pack, then the voice says it. See NINJA. HEAD Words that get longer as you copy them, then two words, then a QSO line. See HEAD.

The device sends at CHAR SPEED, with FARNSWORTH spacing when you set it. See the RECEIVE section in Settings. The RCV value in the header shows the speed, such as 20/20, or 20/10 with Farnsworth spacing.

docs.title: How a drill runs
docs.text:
1. The device sends a group. The state at the right of your copy shows LISTEN.
  2. The state shows YOUR TURN. Start to key what you copied within 5 seconds. You can also start while the group still plays, except in HEAD.
  3. While you key, the state shows KEYING. When you stop keying for three word gaps, your copy ends.
  4. The device scores your copy and shows it in the list. The next group starts after about 1 second.

If you do not start to key within 5 seconds, the group counts as missed when you copy the next one. After two such groups in a row, the drill pauses, and neither group counts: the status line shows NO COPY FOR 2 GROUPS: PAUSED. Key any character, or press F3 (GO), to go on. The character you key does not count as copy.

To hear the group again, key ? alone as your copy.

docs.title: What the screen shows
docs.text:
• The top line: in KOCH, your level and your progress to the next level, such as LEVEL 5 30/50 CHARS 80% NEED 90%: the characters scored at this level, up to the last 50, the percent of them you copied, and the percent the next level needs.
  • The character set, each character in the color of how well you copy it. Green: you know it. Amber: not enough tries to tell. Red, inverted: weak. Gray: not sent yet. KOCH shows the characters of your level, and a line marks the newest one. The other drills show all 44 characters.
  • In HEAD, the top line shows your rung and what it sends, such as RUNG 3 OF 8 1 WORD OF 5 CHARS.
  • The list of recent groups. Each row shows the group that was sent, then your copy with each character marked: green for right, red and inverted for wrong, _ for missed. The score shows at the right, such as 4/5.
  • In HEAD, each item takes two rows: what was sent, then your marked copy under it. The list shows the last 3 items.
  • Your copy as you key it, with the state at the right: LISTEN, YOUR TURN, KEYING or PAUSED.
  • The footer: your score for this session, such as SESSION 85% 120 CHARS. Before your first score, and while you wait to key, it says what to do. While the drill is paused, it says how to go on.

docs.title: NINJA
docs.text:
NINJA works like Morse Code Ninja: the device sends a word, and then the voice says it. You can just listen, or copy it in your head and key it back first.

  1. The device sends a word. The state shows LISTEN.
  2. The state shows YOUR TURN. To be scored, start to key the word within 1.5 seconds.
  3. If you key, the device scores your copy as in the other drills, then the voice says the word.
  4. If you do not key, the voice says the word, and the list shows it with no score.
  5. The next word starts about 1 second after the voice ends.

The words are the ham words and abbreviations of the content pack, then the most common English words: 500 by default. NINJA WORDS in the DRILLS section of the settings sets how many. An abbreviation on its own comes with its meaning: after QTH, the voice says "Q T H. location".

NINJA needs the content pack. Without it, the drill shows CONTENT PACK MISSING: INSTALL IT and sends nothing. Install again, with the content pack.

docs.title: HEAD
docs.text:
HEAD is a head-copy ladder. You copy each item in your head while it plays, and key it back after it ends. Keying while it plays does not count.

Rung What the device sends 1 One word of 2 or 3 characters 2 One word of 4 3 One word of 5 4 One word of 6 5 One word of 7 to 10 6 Two words of 2 to 4 each 7 Two words of 3 to 6 each 8 A line of a QSO, such as NAME BOB BOB or RIG IC7300 100W

Three copies in a row all right move you up one rung. Three copies in a row under half right move you down one. An extra character makes a copy not all right. A ? repeat does not count.

The words come from the content pack: ham words and common English words. HEAD needs the content pack, as NINJA does. The device keeps your rung, also after you turn it off.

docs.title: The Koch method
docs.text:
The KOCH drill starts at level 2, with K and M. You move up one level when you copy at least 90 % right over 50 characters. Each level adds the next character in this order:

K M U R E S N A P T L W I . J Z = F O Y , V G 5 / Q 9 2 H 3 8 B ? 4 7 C 1 D 6 0 X <AR> <SK> <KN>

The score counts extra characters you key as errors, the same as missed ones. After 50 characters below 90 %, the count starts again. When you move up, the status line shows the new character, such as LEVEL UP: ADDED U.

The drill picks weak characters more often, and the newest character twice as often.

The device keeps your level and your progress toward the next level while you use other screens. The level stays after you turn the device off.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Control Action F1 (SET) Pauses the drill and opens the settings at the RECEIVE section, or at DRILLS from NINJA. F4 (BACK) there returns, and the next group plays at the new settings. F2 (AGN) While a group plays or waits for your copy: sends the group again, and clears your copy. Blank while the drill is paused. F3 (STOP or GO) Pauses the drill, or starts it again. While the drill is paused, a character you key also starts it again. F4 (BACK) Pauses the drill and opens the RECEIVE list of the menu. Click the drill or RESUME there to go on. Dial turn Changes the focused header value. See Header values. Dial turn on LEVEL KOCH only: sets your level, 2 to 44. A new level starts its progress count from zero; turn back to the level you left and its count returns. Dial click Moves the focus to the next header value. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Keys your copy.

Your scores also go to Letters and Progress.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: All settings are on one screen, in one list with nine sections: KEYER, SOUND, RECEIVE, DRILLS, QSO, MEMORIES, CALLSIGN, DEVICE and THEME. The device saves the settings 2 seconds after your last change.

docs.title: Open the settings
docs.text:
From Press Opens at section Menu, row SETTINGS Dial click KEYER Menu, KEYER, TIMING F1 (SET) KEYER KOCH, WORDS, CALLS, HEAD, LETTERS, PROGRESS F1 (SET) RECEIVE NINJA, CHEW, QUIZ F1 (SET) DRILLS POTA, SOTA, HUNT F1 (SET) QSO RADIO F1 (SET) DEVICE SYSTEM F1 (SET) THEME

F4 (BACK) leaves the settings and returns to the screen you came from. A drill or a QSO you paused continues. From the SETTINGS row of the menu, F4 (BACK) returns to the menu.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Control Action F1 hold Does what F1 HOLD sets, as on every screen. See Held buttons. F2 (PREV) Selects the first row of the section before. From KEYER, it goes to THEME. F3 (NEXT) Selects the first row of the next section. From THEME, it goes to KEYER. F4 (BACK) Leaves the settings. F4 hold (HOME) Opens the KEYER screen. Dial turn Selects another row. While you edit, changes the value. Dial click Starts or ends editing the selected row. While you edit, the value shows as < value >. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more, except while you edit a memory or your callsign.

Numbers stop at their lowest and highest values. A choice of words goes around: after the last value, the first value comes again.

A line under the list tells you what the selected row sets.

docs.title: KEYER
docs.text: Row Values Default What it sets MODE IAMBIC A, IAMBIC B, STRAIGHT IAMBIC B Your key type. See Keys and jacks. PADDLES NORMAL, REVERSED NORMAL NORMAL: dots on the tip contact. REVERSED: dots on the ring contact. STRAIGHT mode ignores this row. SPEED 5 to 60 WPM 20 WPM Your sending speed. KEY OUT ON, OFF ON Whether your key keys the func jack on the KEYER, TIMING and RADIO screens. See The func jack. OUT TYPE STRAIGHT, PADDLE STRAIGHT STRAIGHT: one line keys, for a radio's straight key input. PADDLE: two lines follow your contacts, for the radio's own keyer. OUT LINES TIP KEYS, RING KEYS (STRAIGHT); DIT ON TIP, DIT ON RING (PADDLE) TIP KEYS or DIT ON TIP Which lines of the func jack key.

docs.title: SOUND
docs.text:
Row Values Default What it sets TONE 300 to 1200 Hz, in steps of 10 Hz 700 Hz The pitch of your sidetone. Other stations send at pitches near it. VOLUME 0 to 44 23 0 is off. Each step is 1.5 dB on headphones and 1 dB on the speaker. WAVE SINE, SQUARE SINE SINE is a pure tone. SQUARE is a buzzier tone with soft edges. NOISE OFF, 1 to 10 OFF Band noise under the stations you hear. FADING OFF, 1 to 10 OFF How deep the stations you hear fade in and out.

Noise and fading play in the receive drills, the ragchew, and on the POTA, SOTA and HUNT screens. While a SOUND row is selected, the band noise plays, so you hear the level you set.

docs.title: RECEIVE
docs.text: Row Values Default What it sets CHAR SPEED MATCH, 5 to 40 WPM MATCH The speed of each character the device sends you: the drills, the ragchew, and the stations of POTA, SOTA and HUNT. MATCH uses your keyer SPEED. FARNSWORTH OFF, 5 to 40 WPM OFF Longer gaps between characters and words, so the text comes at this slower overall speed. It never goes above CHAR SPEED.

docs.title: DRILLS
docs.text: Row Values Default What it sets CHEW SHOWS WHOLE OVER, EACH LINE WHOLE OVER When the ragchew CHEW shows its text. NINJA WORDS 100 to 3000, in steps of 100 500 How many words the NINJA drill picks from: the ham words first, then the most common English words.

docs.title: QSO
docs.text: Row Values Default What it sets PILEUP OFF, TAKE TURNS, OVERLAP TAKE TURNS How the hunters call when you activate. FIST HUMAN, CLEAN HUMAN HUMAN: each station keys with small timing errors. CLEAN: exact timing. SPEED SPREAD ON, OFF ON ON: each hunter or activator sends up to 5 WPM faster or slower than CHAR SPEED.

docs.title: MEMORIES
docs.text:
Row Values M1 to M4 The message, up to 48 characters. A prosign such as <AR> takes 4. REPEAT EVERY The silence between two sends of a held memory: 2 to 30 seconds. The default is 6 seconds. AFTER SEND CLOSE closes the MEM row after a send. STAY OPEN keeps the MEM row open, for one QSO after another.

See Edit the memories.

docs.title: CALLSIGN
docs.text:
CALL is your callsign. The QSO and hunt screens use it, and the boot screen draws it. The default is N0CALL, a placeholder callsign.

Click the dial on CALL, then key your callsign. Each character you key goes at the end. A callsign holds up to 10 characters: letters, digits and /. The device ignores other characters. Click again to end.

Control while you edit Action F2 (DEL) Deletes the last character. F3 hold (CLEAR) Deletes the whole callsign. Dial click Ends editing. Key Adds characters to your callsign.

docs.title: DEVICE
docs.text: Row Values Default What it sets USB OUT OFF, TEXT, VBAND, SERIAL, RADIO OFF What the USB port sends a computer. TEXT types what you key. VBAND sends your keying to VBand. SERIAL is the serial port alone, for a logging program. RADIO types what the decoder board hears, and shows only while DECODER BOARD is ON. See USB keyboard. DECODER BOARD ON, OFF OFF ON: the device powers the decoder board of the Pro model, and the ON AIR list of the menu shows RADIO. RADIO also shows while USB OUT is not OFF, for MIDI in. OFF also changes USB OUT from RADIO to OFF. See Radio. F1 HOLD KEY OUT, RESUME, MEM ROW, TIMING KEY OUT What holding F1 does on every screen. See Held buttons.

docs.title: THEME
docs.text:
Row Values Default What it sets STYLE HAZARD, HUD, BLOCK HAZARD The shapes of the screen: the frame, the header, the button labels and the selection. PALETTE 16 palettes ORANGE The colors of the screen and of the boot screen. BRIGHTNESS 10 % to 100 %, in steps of 10 % 100 % The brightness of the screen.

The palettes are ORANGE, CYAN, AMBER, LIME, DAILY, and the pride flags RAINBOW, TRANS, BI, LESBIAN, PAN, NONBIN, ACE, ARO, FLUID, AGENDER and QUEER. DAILY shows a different flag each time you turn the device on. While you edit STYLE or PALETTE, the whole screen changes as you turn the dial.

The colors that grade your timing are the same in every palette: green, amber and red.

docs.title: Status messages
docs.text: Short messages show on the bottom line of the screen, brighter than the screen's own footer. Most show for 5 seconds, and then the footer comes back. A stuck contact, RELEASE TO POWER OFF and BATTERY EMPTY: POWERING OFF stay until the state ends. In this list, n is a number and X is a character.

docs.title: Power and battery
docs.text:
Message Meaning RELEASE TO POWER OFF You held the dial for 1 second. Let go of the dial to turn the device off, or press an F button or turn the dial to stay on. BATTERY LOW: PLUG IN USB The battery is below 3.4 V. Connect USB power to charge it. BATTERY EMPTY: POWERING OFF The battery is empty. After 2 seconds the device saves everything and turns off.

See System.

docs.title: Saves
docs.text:
Each of these messages means a write to the memory chip failed. The device keeps the values while it is on, but they can be lost when it turns off.

Message What was not saved SETTINGS NOT SAVED Your settings. MEMORIES NOT SAVED Your memories. LETTER STATS NOT SAVED Your letter statistics and Koch level. PROGRESS NOT SAVED This session in Progress. BATTERY CALIBRATION NOT SAVED The full point of the battery gauge.

When a save fails at power off, the device waits 3 seconds before it turns off, so you can read the message. If these messages come again and again, look at the EEPROM row on the System screen.

docs.title: Key and hardware
docs.text: Message Meaning DIT STUCK ON: CHECK PLUG A contact of the key jack stayed closed too long, and stopped keying until it opens. The message names DIT, DAH, TIP or RNG. See Keys and jacks. CODEC DID NOT ANSWER The audio chip did not take a new volume. n INPUTS LOST Button presses, key changes or decoded characters came faster than the screen could handle them, and the device lost n of them. n USB KEYS LOST The device lost n characters, key changes or notes on their way to the computer. See USB keyboard. n SERIAL ERRORS USB refused n reads or writes on the serial port. n SERIAL LINES LOST The serial port had no room for n lines to the computer. The computer was not reading them. SCREENSHOT NOT SENT The computer stopped taking a screenshot for 0.5 s. KEY OUT ON, KEY OUT OFF You held F1 and turned KEY OUT on or off. See Controls. KEY OUT ON: NOT ON THIS SCREEN You held F1 and turned KEY OUT on, on a screen where your key does not key the radio. It keys the radio on the KEYER, TIMING and RADIO screens. NOTHING TO RESUME You held F1 with F1 HOLD set to RESUME, and you have not opened a drill or QSO yet.

docs.title: WinKeyer
docs.text:
These messages show while a logging program uses the device as a WinKeyer. See USB keyboard.

Message Meaning WINKEYER OPEN A logging program took the serial port as a WinKeyer. WINKEYER CLOSED The logging program let the serial port go, or the computer closed it. Text it had not sent yet is dropped. WINKEYER n WPM The logging program set SPEED to n WPM. n WINKEYER BYTES LOST The device dropped n bytes to or from the logging program, because its queue was full.

docs.title: VBand Hotline
docs.text:
These messages show when VBand's page connects to the device as a CW Hotline. See USB keyboard.

Message Meaning HOTLINE ON VBand took the serial port. The device sends your keying to it, and types nothing. HOTLINE OFF VBand let the serial port go, or the browser closed it. VAIL ON Vail's page loaded with the MIDI port. The device sends your keying to it as note 0, and no Ctrl keys. See USB keyboard.

docs.title: Memories
docs.text:
These lines show on the KEYER screen. See Memories. The first four are the footer: they stay while their state lasts, in the footer's color.

Message Meaning HOLD REPEATS CLICK CLOSES The memory row is open. Hold an F button to send its memory again and again. A dial click closes the row. SENDING Mn KEY TO STOP Memory n is sending. Touch your key to stop it. Mn REPEATS EVERY nS KEY TO STOP Memory n waits that long after each send, then sends again. Mn TONE ONLY: OUT TYPE PADDLE or Mn TONE ONLY: KEY OUT OFF Memory n plays as a tone and does not key the func jack. Mn IS EMPTY (SETTINGS) Memory n holds no message. Key one in, in the MEMORIES section of the settings. MEMORY FULL In the settings: the memory has no room for the last character you keyed. A memory holds up to 48 characters, and a prosign such as <AR> takes 4.

docs.title: Practice
docs.text: Message Meaning NO COPY FOR 2 GROUPS: PAUSED Two drill groups in a row passed with no copy, so the drill paused and scored neither. Key a character or press GO to go on. See Receive drills. LEVEL UP: ADDED X You moved up a Koch level, and the drill now sends character X too. See Receive drills.

docs.title: The red error screen
docs.text: If PocketCW finds an error it cannot continue from, the screen turns dark red and shows what went wrong. The func jack and the LED turn off, so a radio does not stay keyed. Click the dial to turn the device off. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Go back to the stock firmware
docs.text: This page puts the original HamCube firmware, version V5.03, back on the device. PocketCW does not include the HamCube files. The install script downloads them from a separate source.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Board 2.64 has a different sound chip (an ES8388). The published stock versions, V5.03 and the beta V5.03.13, have no setup for that chip, so the speaker is silent under them. At least one board 2.64 came from the factory with V5.03.15, a version HamCube has not published, and its sound worked. If your device came with a stock version newer than V5.03.13, you cannot get that version back after you install PocketCW.

Boards from 2.63 have an IPS screen. Stock V5.03 has no setup for the IPS screen, so it shows that screen on its side, in strips. The beta version V5.03.13 sets up the IPS screen, but only on boards that read as version 2.63. No published stock version fully supports board 2.64.

The SYSTEM screen of PocketCW shows your board version on the BOARD row.

Stock firmware keeps its settings in a different part of the memory chip than PocketCW. If you install PocketCW again later, it finds its settings again.

docs.title: The two stock files
docs.text:
The stock firmware is two files from HamCube's V5.03 upgrade package:

  • F0000C0.bin holds the images of the stock screens. The stock firmware draws its screens from the device's image memory, and an older V5.02 copy of this file scrambles the stock screen. PocketCW never reads the image memory, so PocketCW works with any version of this file.
  • A000014.bin is the stock firmware.

Install both files, F0000C0.bin first, as HamCube says. The bootloader can fail an A000014.bin install that comes with no F file before it, and leave the device on the update screen.

PocketCW does not include these files. The install script downloads them from github.com/admvip/CW-Pokemon-Infomation, and checks that each one matches the V5.03 file.

docs.title: Windows and Linux
docs.text:
1. Download F0000C0.bin and A000014.bin from the "CW Pokemon V5.03 Upgrade package" folder of the HamCube files.
  2. Put the device in update mode, and plug it in. The drive opens.
  3. Copy F0000C0.bin to the drive. Wait until the drive closes and opens again with only READY.TXT. Then hold F4 to reset the drive.
  4. Copy A000014.bin to the drive.
  5. Wait about 10 seconds. The drive closes, then opens again with only READY.TXT.
  6. Unplug the device, then click the dial to turn it on.

On Linux, run sync after each copy, so the file goes to the device at once.

docs.title: macOS
docs.text:
Start the script as in Start the script, with this line in place of the PocketCW line:

curl -fsSL https://kvmet.github.io/k5mme_pocketcw/install.sh | sh -s stock

Then:

  1. Follow the steps the script prints. The script installs both files in one update mode session, so you put the device in update mode only once. macOS can ask for your password once for each file.
  2. When the script says "Finished", unplug the device, then click the dial to turn it on.

To install PocketCW again, follow Install.

docs.title: The beta for board 2.63
docs.text:
On a board 2.63, you can use the beta V5.03.13 in place of the V5.03 A000014.bin. The install script does not download the beta.

  1. Install the stock firmware with the steps above, so the device has the V5.03 images.
  2. In the HamCube files, open the folder "CW Pokemon Beta Upgrade package", download V5.03.13Beta.zip, and unzip it. It holds only A000014.bin.
  3. Copy that A000014.bin to the update drive, as in Install. On a Mac, use the install tool below in place of a copy.

On a Mac, download the PocketCW install tool in Terminal, and make it a program you can run:

curl -fsSLo ~/Downloads/pocketcw-flash https://github.com/kvmet/k5mme_pocketcw/releases/latest/download/pocketcw-flash

chmod +x ~/Downloads/pocketcw-flash

Then run the tool on the beta file, and follow the steps it prints. Replace the path with the place of your file:

~/Downloads/pocketcw-flash ~/Downloads/V5.03.13Beta/A000014.bin

docs.title: System
docs.text:
The SYSTEM screen shows the firmware version, the results of the startup checks, and the battery. Open SYSTEM in the menu.

A value in red shows a problem.

docs.title: Rows
docs.text:
Row Example What it shows FIRMWARE v0.2.0 The PocketCW version. BOARD 2.64 IPS AUTO The board version, the kind of screen, and how the device picked the kind of screen. See below. MCU AT32F403A 256K The processor and its flash memory size. CLOCK 72 MHZ XTAL The processor speed and its clock source. XTAL is the crystal. HICK, in red, is the less exact internal clock. CODEC ES8388 OK The audio chip and whether it answered. NONE FOUND means no audio chip answered. EEPROM 24C16 OK The memory chip that holds your settings and statistics. With FAIL, the device cannot save. BATTERY 3.95V 70% 2443 The battery voltage, the charge in percent, and the raw reading. With USB power, it shows USB and the voltage. Red when the battery is low. SUPPLY 3.29V The voltage the processor runs on. UPTIME 0:12:05 Hours, minutes and seconds since the device turned on. BOOTS 57 How many times PocketCW started.

ADC FAIL in BATTERY and SUPPLY means the device could not read the voltages.

Under the rows, two small lines show what the screen answered on pins B4 and B5 when the device asked for its ID (FLOAT means no answer), and the unique ID of the processor. These help when you report a problem.

docs.title: How the device picks the kind of screen
docs.text:
BOARD shows The kind of screen comes from AUTO The board version. ID The ID the screen gave. SET Your choice: you held F2 when you turned the device on. NOSAVE, in red You held F2 when you turned the device on, but the device could not save the choice.

To change the kind of screen, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Battery
docs.text:
The battery icon at the right end of the header shows the charge:

Icon Meaning Plus sign USB power. 1 to 4 bars The charge, in quarters. Red outline, no bars The battery is low.

The device learns where full charge reads on your battery. A battery gauge reads a little differently on each board. The device takes a new full point when the battery reads higher than before, after 2 minutes without USB power. The full point stays within 3 % of the design value. The device saves the full point.

When the battery goes below 3.4 V, the status line says BATTERY LOW: PLUG IN USB. When the battery stays below 3.2 V, or the supply below 3.1 V, for 10 seconds, the status line says BATTERY EMPTY: POWERING OFF. After 2 seconds, the device saves everything and turns off.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1 (SET) Opens the settings at the THEME section. F4 (BACK) there returns to this screen. F2, F3 Nothing. F4 (BACK) Opens the menu, with SYSTEM selected. Dial turn Changes the focused header value. See Header values. Dial click Moves the focus to the next header value. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Nothing more.

docs.title: Timing
docs.text:
The TIMING screen gives a close look at your keying. Open it with F3 (TMNG) on the KEYER screen, or from the menu. The header shows TIMING, the keyer mode, and the SND and VOL values.

The screen measures every mark and gap against the dot length the decoder uses: the dot length of your set speed in the iambic modes, or of the speed you actually send in STRAIGHT mode. A unit is that dot length. The screen grades each mark and gap as good, off or bad. See Timing grades.

docs.title: Zoomed tape
docs.text:
The tape draws time from left to right, 8 pixels per dot length.

  • The SET row shows brackets around the ideal length of each mark.
  • The YOU row shows each mark you sent, in the color and shape of its grade. A good mark is solid, an off mark has a stripe through it, and a bad mark is an outline.
  • Over each mark, a number shows its error in percent: +10 is 10 % long, -10 is 10 % short.
  • Under the marks, each decoded character shows, and each gap between characters or words shows its length in units.
  • A gap inside a character that is off or bad gets an underline in its grade.

Under the tape, F3 switches between two views: BARS, and HAND.

docs.title: BARS view
docs.text:
Histogram Range Dotted lines at MARKS 0 to 4 units 1 (dot) and 3 (dash) GAPS 0 to 8 units 1 (inside a character), 3 (between characters) and 7 (between words)

Each bar counts the marks or gaps of that length, in the color of the grade a mark or gap of that length gets.

Line What it shows DIT Average dot length and its standard deviation (SD) in milliseconds, then RATIO: average dash over average dot. The ideal ratio is 3. DAH Average dash length and its standard deviation in milliseconds, then the speed your timing works out to. GAP, CHR, WRD Average gap inside characters, between characters and between words, in units.

docs.title: HAND view
docs.text:
The HAND view shows what your paddle or key does, not what the keyer sends. It shows the statistics for the MODE in use.

In IAMBIC A and IAMBIC B, the keyer decides one unit after each element whether to send another. A paddle closed at that moment, or pressed during the element, sends one.

Item What it shows RELEASE BEFORE THE KEYER DECIDES A histogram from 0 to 3 units: at the end of each character, how long before the keyer's decision you let go. A bar under half a unit is red: a little later, and the keyer would have sent one more element. RELEASE The average and standard deviation of that time, in units. CLOSE The percent of characters you let go less than half a unit before the decision, and how many characters it counts. LATE The percent of gaps inside characters you started after the keyer's decision, how many gaps it counts, and how late they came on average, in units. A late press makes a gap longer than one unit. LATE counts only the gaps that still read as inside a character; a press late enough to split the character shows as a short gap between characters in the BARS view.

In STRAIGHT, for a straight key or a sideswiper:

Line What it shows TIP, RING For each contact, the average length and standard deviation of the dots and dashes it keyed, in milliseconds. A mark counts for the contact that closed first. A straight key uses only the tip. WEIGHT Each dot over the gap after it inside a character, on average, with its standard deviation. 1.00 is even; more is heavy, less is light. RATIO For each contact, its average dash over its average dot. 3.0 is standard. OVERLAP The percent of marks during which the other contact closed too, and how many marks it counts. On a sideswiper, the second contact holds the key down, so the mark runs long.

Keying that SEND sends over USB counts in BARS, but not in HAND.

The statistics collect your keying on every screen since the device was turned on, or since you last held F2 (CLEAR). The KEYER screen shows the BARS statistics.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Control Action F1 (SET) Opens the settings at the KEYER section. F2 hold (CLEAR) Clears the statistics and the tape. F3 (HAND or BARS) Switches the view under the tape. F4 (BACK) Opens the menu, with TIMING selected. Dial turn Changes the focused header value. See Header values. Dial click Moves the focus to the next header value. Dial hold Turns the device off. Key Draws on the tape and adds to the statistics.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page lists install problems first, then problems on the device.

docs.title: Install messages
docs.text: These messages come from the macOS install tool. When it finds a problem, it prints Problem: and one of these messages, then waits. Do what the message says, press Return, and follow the steps the tool prints again.

docs.title: "could not download"
docs.text: The script could not reach GitHub. Check that the Mac is connected to the internet, and run the line from Start the script again.

docs.title: "the update drive is mounted"
docs.text: The device was in update mode before the script started, so macOS opened its drive. Eject the drive in Finder. Its name is POKEMON-2 or HAM MODULE. Unplug the device, and press Return.

docs.title: "no update drive appeared in 180 seconds"
docs.text:
The Mac did not find the device in update mode. Check these two things:

  • The device showed the firmware update screen before you plugged it in. See Update mode.
  • The cable carries data. Try another cable or another USB port.

Then press Return.

docs.title: "macOS did not allow writing to the device"
docs.text: The password box was closed with Cancel. Press Return, and type your Mac login password when macOS asks. If the box shakes, the password was wrong: type it again.

docs.title: "the device status is ..., not Ready"
docs.text: The update drive is not ready to take a file. Hold F4, which resets the drive, then press Return. If the message comes back, unplug the device and press Return.

docs.title: "the drive already holds a file"
docs.text: macOS wrote something to the drive before the install tool could stop it. Hold F4 to reset the drive, then press Return.

docs.title: "the status stayed Ready for 10 s; the device did not take the file"
docs.text: The write did not finish. Press Return to install again.

docs.title: "the device dropped off USB before showing Success"
docs.text: The tool cannot tell whether the write finished. Press Return to install again.

docs.title: "the device status is ..., not Success"
docs.text: The device reported a problem with the file. Press Return to install again. If the message comes back, report it on the issue tracker with the status the message shows.

docs.title: "is not the V5.03 file this script expects"
docs.text: The script restores the stock firmware only from the exact V5.03 files. The downloaded file is different, so the script stopped before it changed anything. Report it on the issue tracker.

docs.title: The device shows the update screen when you only want to use it
docs.text:
If the battery is full and the device is plugged into USB, it sometimes starts in update mode. Unplug USB and click the dial to turn it on.

If the device starts in update mode every time, even unplugged, the last install did not finish. Install again, with the content pack.

docs.title: The screen is turned on its side, or shows the picture in strips
docs.text:
Boards use one of two kinds of screen, and the firmware cannot always tell which one it has. To switch to the other kind:

  1. Hold the dial down for about 2 seconds. The device turns off, even though you cannot read the screen.
  2. Hold F2 down. F2 is the second button from the top.
  3. While you hold F2, click the dial to turn the device on.
  4. Let go of F2 when the screen shows a picture.

The device remembers the choice. To switch back, do the same steps again.

docs.title: The device does not start after an install
docs.text: Run the install again from step 1. The install never changes the bootloader, so update mode always works.

docs.title: A red screen with an error
docs.text: The firmware stopped on an error it cannot recover from. Click the dial to turn the device off. Then turn it on again. If the error comes back, copy the text on the screen into a report on the issue tracker.

docs.title: No sound
docs.text: Check the volume: the VOL value on the KEYER screen, or VOLUME in the SOUND section of the settings. At 0 the sound is off. A plug in the headphone jack turns the speaker off.

docs.title: A message on the bottom line of the screen
docs.text: See Status messages.

docs.title: USB keyboard
docs.text:
The device can show up on a computer, phone or tablet as a USB keyboard, a MIDI port and a serial port. Set USB OUT in the DEVICE section of the settings.

USB OUT What the computer gets OFF Nothing. The USB port only charges the battery. This is the default. TEXT Each character you key, typed as text. VBAND Your keying as the Ctrl keys, for VBand. SERIAL No typing. A logging program uses the serial port as a WinKeyer. RADIO Each character the decoder board of the Pro model hears, typed as text.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
1. Turn the device on.
  2. Plug the USB cable into the device and the computer.

The computer finds a keyboard named PocketCW. It needs no driver. The first time, macOS can open its Keyboard Setup Assistant. Close it.

If the device is plugged into USB when you turn it on, it can start in update mode. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: TEXT
docs.text:
The device types each character that the decoder reads from your key. Use it with any program that takes typed text, such as a copy trainer or a text editor.

  • A character types after the gap that ends it, as it shows on the screen.
  • A word gap types one space.
  • Letters type in lowercase.
  • A pattern that is not a character types *. A prosign types between angle brackets, such as <AR>, as on the screen.
  • It works on every screen, with every key type.

docs.title: Keyboard layout
docs.text:
The device sends the keys of a US keyboard, and the computer turns each key into a character with its own layout setting.

  • With a US layout, every character types correctly.
  • With another layout, letters and digits are mostly correct, but punctuation such as /, ?, @ and " can type other characters. Some layouts also exchange Y and Z.

For exact text, set the computer's keyboard layout to US.

docs.title: Phones and tablets
docs.text: While a USB keyboard is connected, an iPhone or iPad hides its on-screen keyboard. To charge the device from a phone or tablet, set USB OUT to OFF.

docs.title: RADIO
docs.text:
The device types each character that it decodes from the decoder board. The text types the same way as TEXT, and your keying types nothing.

  • USB OUT offers RADIO only while DECODER BOARD is ON. If you set DECODER BOARD to OFF, USB OUT changes to OFF.
  • The device decodes the board on every screen, not only on the RADIO screen.

docs.title: VBAND
docs.text:
VBAND sends your keying the way the VBand USB adapter does. In VBand, set the key type to match MODE in the KEYER section of the settings.

MODE The device sends Set VBand to IAMBIC A, IAMBIC B The dot lever holds Left Ctrl, and the dash lever holds Right Ctrl. PADDLES sets which lever is which. An iambic paddle. VBand times the elements with its own keyer. STRAIGHT Left Ctrl, held while the device keys. This works for a straight key and a sideswiper. A straight key.

docs.title: VBand CW Hotline
docs.text:
VBand's page can also take your keying over the serial port, as it does from a CW Hotline. VBand does not document this, so a change to VBand can stop it.

  1. Plug the device into a computer. USB OUT can be any setting but OFF.
  2. Open VBand in Chrome, Edge, or Firefox 151 or later. Safari cannot open a serial port.
  3. Click Connect to CW Hotline, and choose the PocketCW port.

The screen shows HOTLINE ON when VBand connects, and HOTLINE OFF when it disconnects or the browser closes the port.

  • The device sends what keys the radio: your keying, SEND text from the serial port, and memories.
  • While VBand has the port, the device types nothing and sends no Ctrl keys, so VBand never gets your keying twice.
  • VBand sends nothing back. You hear the other stations from VBand, not from the device.
  • VBand passes your keying to a channel only while another station is in it. The Practice Channel and the Lobby do not pass it on.
  • A space longer than 3 seconds goes to VBand as 3 seconds. VBand takes that as the start of a new over.
  • If HOTLINE ON never shows, the browser has no serial port support, or VBand changed how it connects.

docs.title: MIDI
docs.text:
Every USB OUT setting but OFF also has a MIDI port named PocketCW. It sends what keys the radio as notes: your keying, SEND text from the serial port, and memories.

  • Each mark is one Note On and one Note Off, on channel 1 at full velocity.
  • The note is the one nearest your TONE setting, so a synthesizer or music program plays your keying at your sidetone pitch.

Notes the computer sends sound on the device at their own pitch, and the RADIO screen decodes them.

  • The tone sounds while any note is held. Two stations at once sound as one tone, at the pitch of the newer note, and decode as garble.
  • A tone longer than 3 seconds stops, so a lost Note Off cannot hold the speaker on.
  • The device ignores every message but Note On and Note Off.

docs.title: Vail
docs.text:
Vail takes your keying from the MIDI port, as it does from the Vail adapter.

  1. Plug the device into a computer. USB OUT can be any setting but OFF.
  2. Open Vail in Chrome or Edge, and allow it to use MIDI devices.

The screen shows VAIL ON when Vail's page loads. Until you unplug the device or set USB OUT to OFF:

  • The device sends note 0, which Vail reads as a straight key in every one of its keyer modes. Every MODE works, since the device times the elements.
  • In VBAND, the device sends no Ctrl keys, so Vail never gets your keying twice.

The other stations in your Vail room sound on the device, and RADIO decodes them.

Keep the Vail tab in front: Chrome slows the timers of a hidden tab.

docs.title: WinKeyer
docs.text:
A logging program can key through the device as if it were a K1EL WinKeyer. The program sends text, and the device keys it on the func jack and the sidetone. Every setting but OFF has the serial port, but SERIAL types nothing, so it is the one to use.

  1. Set USB OUT to SERIAL.
  2. Plug the device into the computer.
  3. In the logging program, choose a WinKeyer on the device's serial port. It is /dev/cu.usbmodem and a number on macOS, /dev/ttyACM and a number on Linux, and a COM port on Windows. The baud rate does not matter.

The screen shows WINKEYER OPEN when the program takes the port, and WINKEYER CLOSED when it lets go.

  • The text keys at the program's speed. When the program sets a speed, SPEED in the KEYER section of the settings changes to it and is saved.
  • The text keys the func jack only when KEY OUT is ON and OUT TYPE is STRAIGHT.
  • Touch your key to stop the program's text. Your keying goes to the radio as usual, and the device tells the program you broke in.
  • The device sends back each character it keys, and each character you key, when the program asks for that.
  • Tune from the program holds the key down.
  • When you change SPEED on the device, the program sees the new speed, as from a WinKeyer's speed knob.
  • If the program asks for WinKeyer pushbuttons, F1 to F4 are the WinKeyer's four buttons, which the program can map to its macros. Until the program lets go, the screen does not see F1 to F4; the dial still works.
  • Your MODE, PADDLES, TONE and VOLUME settings stay in force. The device ignores the program's settings for these, and for weight, PTT, lead-in, Farnsworth and the WinKeyer's own message memories.

docs.title: Status message
docs.text: n USB KEYS LOST means the device lost n characters, key changes or notes on their way to the computer. See Status messages.
